Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the GlobalBank Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, the Q&A session will follow the standard process with instructions provided at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review GlobalBank Holdings's results for the third quarter. With me this morning are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Credit Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Operating Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Marketing Officer; and Thomas Grant, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. GlobalBank Holdings delivered record results in the third quarter, exceeding all previous benchmarks and solidifying our position as a leader in the financial services industry.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Sustaining strong revenue growth
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand reputation
7. Promoting a diverse and inclusive culture
8. Delivering superior returns to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights. On revenue diversification, we've shifted our mix toward resilient fee-based streams, with non-interest income now at 48% of total revenue, up significantly and ahead of targets. Deposit costs averaged 3.92%, navigating competitive pressures effectively while growing total deposits 7.2% year-over-year with a balanced mix. Credit quality is strong, with NPL ratio at 1.18%, down sequentially. NII grew 6% quarter-over-quarter despite a modest year-over-year dip. Fee income broke out across wealth management, investment banking, and cards. We're advancing capital returns with a dividend hike and buybacks. And our guidance rests on solid assumptions like a soft landing and rate cuts.

I will now turn the call over to David Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

David Chen:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning. GlobalBank Holdings reported net income of $2.1 billion for the third quarter, or $1.65 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Total revenue reached $14.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year or 11% adjusted excluding prior FDIC assessments. Let me turn to our revenue diversification initiatives, a cornerstone of our strategy over the past three years. In this volatile environment of interest rate swings, geopolitical challenges, and digital shifts, we've moved away from cyclical NII toward stable fee streams, derisking our P&L and boosting earnings stability, much like peers JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America.

Non-interest income now makes up 48% of total revenue, up from 38% in Q3 2021, beating our 2025 target early. Fee income has compounded at 15% annually since then, outpacing NII by 2.5 times, with our fee-to-total ratio at 2.1 times the industry median per S&P Global.

Key pillars include wealth and asset management, where AUM hit $1.8 trillion, up 22% quarter-over-quarter with $28 billion net new money from high-net-worth clients. Recurring fees reached $2.1 billion, up 19% YoY, margins at 42% via our GlobalWealth Digital platform and WealthAI engine boosting cross-sell to 3.2 products per client. North America drove 72% of growth, APAC 35% via Hong Kong and Tencent partnerships.

Payments and transaction services exploded to $3.4 billion, 25% up YoY, 24% of revenue. GlobalPay processed 4.2 billion transactions, revenue per transaction $0.81, with APIs embedded in Stripe and Plaid ecosystems, unlocking $450 million in treasury fees. EMEA grew 32% on SEPA Instant.

CIB advisory fees rose 14% to $1.2 billion despite M&A slowdowns, with 7.2% share in mid-market deals, including a $18 billion telco merger and $2.5 billion green bond. Equity underwriting up 40% QoQ. LatAm added 28% via Brazil infrastructure.

Emerging areas like ESG products and embedded finance contributed $850 million, up 45%, with $120 billion ESG commitments and blockchain trade finance cutting times 70%.

This mix added 420 bps to ROE at 14.2%, lowered volatility, and preserves EPS in stress scenarios. Regions: North America 62%, EMEA 22%, APAC 12%, LatAm 4%. Forward, 16-18% fee growth in 2025, CET1 11.8%, 10% dividend hike.

Net interest income increased 6% quarter-over-quarter to $2.52 billion from $2.38 billion, though down 3% YoY from $2.60 billion. Full-year NII at $9.85 billion, down 1%. NIM expanded 10 bps QoQ to 3.48%, down 7 bps YoY.

QoQ growth from loan expansion to $285 billion, yields up in CIB to 5.85%; stable deposits at $320 billion, costs up just 8 bps to 2.45%; securities yields up. YoY decline from funding costs to 2.35%, betas at 65%.

Regions: North America up 2%, Europe down 12% on ECB hikes, APAC flat.

Turning to deposits, our base grew 7.2% YoY to $285 billion, core up 6.8%, ninth straight quarter of organic growth. Transactional at 42%, $119.7 billion up 3.1% YoY, low beta 12%. Savings 38%, $108.3 billion up 12.4%, rates at 4.65%. Time 20%, $56.9 billion up 18.7%.

Strategies: digital app with AI optimizers, loyalty programs, embedded finance. Q4 growth 2-3%.

Cost of deposits averaged 3.92%, up 18 bps QoQ, 152 bps YoY, beta 45%. Non-interest-bearing 28% at 0%, interest-bearing 4.68%. Competitive from Ally, SoFi, big banks. Tech pricing engine, cross-sell, Deposit Shield program. Q3 up 10-15 bps.

Fee income totaled $4.8 billion full-year, up 14%, 28% of non-interest revenue. Wealth management $2.1 billion up 18%, AUM $2.7 trillion, $180 billion net new. Investment banking $1.5 billion up 12%, advisory $850 million. Cards $1.2 billion up 9%, TPV $1.1 trillion.

Capital returns: CET1 12.8%, dividend up 10% to $1.05 quarterly, payout 38%. Buybacks $2.8 billion YTD, $7.2 billion remaining, total returns $5.1 billion YTD.

Guidance: FY2024 EPS $6.45-6.65, 2025 growth 7-9%. Assumes GDP 2.3-2.6%, unemployment 4.4%, two rate cuts, NCOs 42-48 bps, loans 4.5-5.5%, fees +8-10%, OpEx +4-5%.

We are generating strong returns on equity and are committed to delivering value to our shareholders.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, David. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate volatility, commercial real estate exposure, geopolitical tensions, and cybersecurity threats. We are implementing enhanced controls and monitoring to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

Robert Kline:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains excellent with NPL ratio at 1.18%, down 12 bps sequentially and 28 bps YoY, below peer 1.45%. Delinquencies at 2.04%, down 21 bps QoQ. Net charge-offs 0.42%, flat QoQ, below 0.50% target.

Consumer NPLs 1.05%, C&I 1.35%, CRE 1.85%. Criticized loans down 25% to 4.2%. AI underwriting, collections hub, ACL 1.42%. Expect NPLs low-1%, charge-offs 0.40-0.45%.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are leveraging technology to enhance customer experience, improve efficiency, and drive innovation. Our investments in AI personalization and blockchain platforms are yielding significant results, like WealthAI and trade finance reductions.

Mark Thompson:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include streamlining our processes, optimizing our infrastructure, and leveraging data analytics to improve decision-making, targeting efficiency ratio improvements.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you. From a marketing perspective, we are focused on strengthening our brand reputation and enhancing customer engagement. Our recent marketing campaigns have been highly successful in driving customer acquisition and retention through digital channels and loyalty programs.

Thomas Grant:
Good morning. We are committed to maintaining the highest standards of compliance and ethical conduct. We are continuously strengthening our compliance programs and working closely with regulators to ensure we are meeting all applicable requirements, including PSD3 and DORA preparations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, as a reminder, that is digit 1 for questions. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez:
Good morning. Could you please provide more detail on revenue diversification initiatives and impact?

Michael Reynolds:
Thanks, John. As David touched on, diversification has been transformative. We've grown non-interest income to 48% of revenue via WAM, payments, CIB, and emerging areas. AUM $1.8T with $28B NNM, payments $3.4B on 4.2B transactions, advisory $1.2B, ESG $850M. This boosts ROE 420 bps, reduces beta to 0.4x GDP, with regional balance mitigating risks. Outlook 16-18% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What is your outlook for deposit growth and mix?

David Chen:
Great question, Emily. Deposits up 7.2% YoY to $285B, transactional 42%, savings 38% surging 12.4%, time 20% up 18.7%. Strategies like AI mobile app, loyalty cross-sell, embedded finance drive Q4 2-3% QoQ growth, stabilizing mix as rates plateau, supporting NIM 3.40-3.55%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of credit quality metrics?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, Alex. Though Robert covered the headlines, NPLs at 1.18% excluding guarantees 0.92%, delinquencies 2.04%, charge-offs 0.42%. Portfolio: consumer 1.05%, CRE 1.85% with low LTV. Regional strength in Midwest, proactive AI interventions cut criticized 25%. Reserves cover 120% NPLs, ready for cycles.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Singh with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Laura Singh:
What are your plans for NII trends going forward?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, Laura. While financials lead here, tech supports NII stability. But from David's details, QoQ +6% to $2.52B on loans, deposits, hedges. YoY -3% from betas, but troughing Q1 2025 with cuts, targeting 2-4% growth via digital deposits, asset optimization, private credit.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Michael Reynolds for any closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in GlobalBank Holdings. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
